title: Conceptualizing the Self in Modern Psychology
text:
Psychology views the self not as a monolithic entity, but as an evolving construct influenced by biological, social, and cognitive factors. Key theories delineate between the 'I' (the perceiver) and the 'Me' (the role played), suggesting that identity formation is a continuous negotiation between internal experience and external expectation.

Furthermore, the concept incorporates multiple self-schemas—mental frameworks derived from past experiences that dictate how an individual anticipates social interaction. These schemas are continually modified through therapeutic processes and exposure to novel environments, challenging rigid assumptions about one's fixed nature.
